subject: Dedicated: transient headroom credits and autoscale policy for NeuroFleet launch
messages:
From: Elaine Zhao <elaine.zhao@neurofleet.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: launch-ops@neurofleet.ai
Date: 2028-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity ask for product launch (Jun 28)

Hi Karthik —

Quick intro: NeuroFleet is ramping to a public beta for our routing product on Jun 28. We expect a very spiky usage profile during the first 72 hours (load tests show 6x baseline for short bursts). We are evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and want to confirm burst/runway behavior: how many transient GPUs can we request, what are eviction policies, and can we get short-term crediting for the launch window?

Attached is a rough traffic model (CSV in the sheet) and the tentative canary rollout plan. Key asks:
- Temporary headroom of +4 p100-equivalent GPUs for up to 36 hours per day over the launch weekend
- Guaranteed cold-start latency <200ms 95th for our primary route
- A clear eviction/fairness policy so we can design client-side backoff

Can we schedule a call this week to lock the playbook?

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Zhao
Head of Platform
NeuroFleet

Attachments: neurofleet_burst_schedule_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Zhao <elaine.zhao@neurofleet.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask for product launch (Jun 28)

Hi Elaine — great to hear about the launch, congrats.

We can absolutely support transient headroom for a launch like this. High level proposal:
- Reserve: we recommend a small baseline dedicated slab sized for steady-state (you mentioned baseline 10 GPUs).
- Elastic runway: we can commit to providing +4 GPUs in the dedicated pool for 36-hour windows over the weekend, subject to a pre-booked runway window and a short uplift fee (one-time transient credit).
- Eviction/fairness: bursts will be backed by a shoulder pool with proportional preemption. We will provide soft preemption (5 minute drain notice) for long-running jobs; for inference routes we will prioritize low-latency lanes and throttle best-effort batch.

Ben — can you draft the technical guardrails (eviction, throttle thresholds, and suggested autoscale policy) for NeuroFleet? Monica — can you outline the commercial uplift/crediting and a short SOW for the transient runway?

Elaine — will plan for a 45-min working session on Thu 2028-05-31 10:00 PT unless you prefer another slot.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-05-31T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask for product launch (Jun 28) — tech guardrails and autoscale draft

Hi team / Elaine,

Thanks for the call earlier — summarizing the technical recommendations and attached a draft playbook (redwood_dedicated_playbook_v3.pdf) and the updated burst schedule. Key points:

1) Baseline sizing
- Keep baseline dedicated slab at 12 A100-equivalent GPUs. That covers steady-state + small growth window.

2) Transient runway (bursting)
- We can offer +4 GPUs as requested, but to make this resilient across other tenants we implement:
  * Scheduled runway windows (you must pre-book windows at least 72 hours in advance)
  * A pooled shoulder of ephemeral GPUs that is replenished hourly
  * Uplift: first 8 hours/day of runway are included as trial credit; hours beyond that are billed at transient rate (we'll set a discounted transient rate for launch customers)

3) Autoscale policy (suggested defaults)
- Scale-up trigger: sustained 90th latency breach for 60s OR queue depth > 50 requests for 30s
- Scale-down: idle for 300s and average token utilization < 35%
- Max transient scale factor: 1.5x baseline (enforced unless pre-approved)

4) Eviction & fairness
- Priority lanes: real-time inference routes get higher priority; batch and background reranking are preemptible.
- Preemption mode: graceful drain with 5-minute 'drain' signal; if job doesn't yield, force preempt at 15 minutes.

5) Observability & runbook
- We will enable per-route tracing and a dedicated launch dashboard (token-level cost, latency percentiles, GPU occupancy).
- We include an ops playbook for throttling / automatic fallback to smaller model variants if latency spikes.

Attachments included:
- redwood_dedicated_playbook_v3.pdf (playbook w/ runbook steps)
- neurofleet_burst_schedule_v1.xlsx (updated)

Next steps:
- Monica: share the commercial uplift sketch and transient credit mechanics.
- Elaine: confirm the exact 36-hour windows you want pre-booked and sign the MOP (attached draft).

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_playbook_v3.pdf (PDF), neurofleet_burst_schedule_v1.xlsx (XLSX)

Subject: Re: Dedicated: transient headroom credits and autoscale policy for NeuroFleet launch — confirmed windows and next steps

Elaine — thanks for confirming the 36-hour windows (Jun 28 00:00 PT — Jun 29 12:00 PT and a fallback window Jul 4 00:00 PT — Jul 5 12:00 PT). To summarize what we agreed internally and what I'll put in the draft SOW: 

- Baseline: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (steady-state).
- Transient runway: +4 GPUs per requested window. First 8 hours/day included as launch credit; beyond that transient uplift fee applies.
- Autoscale policy: use Ben's defaults, with a max transient scale factor of 1.5x unless we sign an expanded commit.
- Eviction: graceful drain notice (5m) then force preempt at 15m for non-low-latency lanes. Real-time lanes pinned to the low-latency queue.
- Observability: dedicated launch dashboard + token-level traces enabled for the two windows.

Attached: signed-mop-draft.docx (placeholders for runway windows & uplift). If this looks right I will route a short SOW and DocuSign for the transient credit terms by EOD Monday.

Action items:
- Elaine: sign off on SOW fields for windows and accept uplift sketch (reply OK).
- Monica: prepare commercial MOP and transient invoice line item.
- Ben: finalize the autoscale params and add the emergency fallback (model variant) to the runbook.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
